name: dag
title: DAG
description: Run a DAG over the mods. The fleet is hundreds of modules and, through the MCP hub, hundreds of tools — every one of them a single call, with nothing that composes them. A graph here is JSON: steps that call an MCP tool on any server the hub carries (the default kind), a mod fn, or an HTTP route, plus declarative `expr` steps that filter, sort, cut and reshape data between two tools so a composition never has to leave the fleet. Steps reference each other with ${...}, and those references ARE the edges — nothing declares a dependency, the graph is built from what the steps actually want, and anything independent runs at the same time. `foreach` fans one step out over a list, in parallel, results in order. Before any of it costs a call, `plan` checks every tool name and every required argument against the live fleet, offers the closest real names for a tool that does not exist, and prices the run in calls and waves. A step that fails does not stop a branch that never depended on it: what is downstream is skipped and each skip names the step that caused it. Graphs are saved by name, every run is written to disk as it goes, and the same nine operations answer over REST, over MCP, and in a browser console on one port.
route_note: deliberately unrouted. A graph step can call any tool in the fleet, including the ones that sign transactions, and the MCP hub trusts a caller on this box — so a dag server on a public port is a way to spend that trust from outside it. Reach it over an SSH tunnel, or set ~/.mod/dag/server.secret and route it behind that.
backend: dagsrc/api.py (stdlib http.server — REST, MCP and the console on one port, no dependencies)

depends.mcp: orbit/mcp at :50360 aggregates the fleet's MCP servers; every `mcp` step is routed through it, and it is what wakes a scaled-to-zero module mid-run. A step with an explicit url= talks MCP directly and needs no hub.

state: ~/.mod/dag — graphs/<name>.json (saved graphs), runs/<id>.json (one record per run, written as it goes), server.secret (optional)

info.docs: The spec of a graph, every field a step accepts, and a complete worked example

health.docs: Liveness, and whether the MCP hub is answering — without it, only steps with an explicit url= can run

run.docs: {graph, inputs?, dry_run?, verbose?} — graph is a saved name or the whole spec. Returns the run record: per-step status, duration, output, and for a failure the cause and everything skipped because of it

plan.docs: {graph, inputs?} — parse, find cycles, infer the edges, check every tool name and required argument against the live fleet, and price the run in calls and waves. Calls nothing

tools.docs: ?q=&server=&limit=&full= — every MCP tool in the fleet under the exact server__tool name a step should use, with the arguments it takes and requires

servers.docs: The fleet's MCP servers, which are answering, and how many tools each carries

graphs.docs: GET: every saved graph. POST {name, graph}: save one — parsed first, so a spec that cannot run is never stored

graph.docs: One saved graph with its execution plan drawn as text; DELETE removes it and keeps its run records

run_record.docs: One run in full. The record is written as the run goes, so this also follows one still in flight

mcp.auth: dag_run, dag_save and dag_delete take the same gate as the REST routes
mcp.docs: MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 (Streamable HTTP), the same nine tools the REST routes call

console.docs: Browser console: search the fleet's tools, click one to add a step, plan it, dry-run it, run it, watch the steps land

mcp.recursion: this module's own tools are aggregated by the hub, so a graph can contain a step that runs a graph. Depth travels with the request as X-Dag-Depth and stops at DAG_MAX_DEPTH

graph.name: a name
graph.steps: the list; the order it is written in does not matter, the references do
graph.output: optional — what the run returns. Without it, the run returns the leaf steps
graph.max_parallel: how many steps may be in flight at once (default 8)

step.id: how other steps refer to it
step.tool: server__tool — an MCP tool. This is the default kind of step
step.url: an MCP endpoint to talk to directly, bypassing the hub
step.call: "<mod>/<fn>" — call a mod fn in-process instead of a tool
step.use: mcp | mod | http | expr | graph — inferred from the fields above
step.args: the call arguments; ${...} anywhere inside them
step.foreach: a list — run this step once per item, in parallel, with ${item} and ${index} bound
step.if / unless: skip the step unless the condition is truthy
step.needs: extra dependencies, for the rare step that must wait for one it does not reference
step.pick: a path into the result — store only that part
step.where / sort_by / desc / limit: filter and cut a list result
step.retries / retry_delay / timeout: per step; a refusal that will refuse again is not retried
step.continue_on_error: a failure here does not fail the run

refs.${x.y?}: missing is null instead of an error
refs.${list.field}: that field over every element of a list

auth.reads: open — the tool catalogue, saved graphs, run history, and dry_run, which spends nothing
auth.writes: running, saving and deleting need Bearer ~/.mod/dag/server.secret, or a caller on this box that is not being proxied (an X-Forwarded-* header counts as remote)
auth.why: a graph can call any tool in the fleet and the hub trusts this box; an ungated runner would launder that trust

env.DAG_MCP_HUB: the MCP hub every mcp step is routed through (default http://127.0.0.1:50360)
env.DAG_ACTIVATOR_URL: scale-to-zero proxy used to reach a mod fn that will not import here (default http://127.0.0.1:9000)
env.MOD_ROOT: where the fleet lives, for `mod` steps (default /root/mod/mod)
env.DAG_MAX_DEPTH: how deep a graph may call a graph (default 3)
env.DAG_KEEP_RUNS: run records kept before the oldest are dropped (default 500)
env.DAG_MAX_RESULT_CHARS: cap on the outputs returned to an MCP caller (default 40000)
